subject: Perk registry
notes: Level costs, gates and every line of effect text are transcribed from the in-game skill screens; the wording is verbatim.
Tree positions, prerequisite links and upgrade-level counts were read from in-game skill screens.
Node names were resolved by matching each in-game icon against the named perk icon set, then verified by eye.
`active_time` is recorded per perk: ANYTIME, DAY ONLY or NIGHT ONLY, exactly as the banner above the perk name reads. It is not uniform within a tree - Witchcraft mixes ANYTIME and DAY ONLY.

Gates are per level, read from the icon on each level row: a book means that level needs a manual, a plain diamond means skill points only. `road shrine` is a gate the published sources do not list at all.

A level row whose cost is hidden in game is one the capture's save had already bought; those costs are kept from the Game8 cross-check rather than guessed. Ownership itself is never recorded - it is save state, not perk data.
Some levels cost skill points but no time segments, so `time_segments` can be 0. The published tables list a time segment everywhere.
Some sources list two rows both labelled 'Lv. 3'. The second is Lv. 4; in-game pips confirm four slots on those perks.
Font of Life and Mandrake Ward are padlocked '?' nodes with no skill point or time cost - story or quest unlocks.
Vampirism ultimates are gated by Corruption 15 alone; only Witchcraft and Swordmastery show the 35-point spend counter.
Where the registry knowingly departs from the Game8 page, source_overrides records the field and the reason.

`text_source` records where each level row's text came from: `game` (read from the in-game panel), `game8` (still the Game8 table, never re-read from the game), or `placeholder` (a padlocked story node that prints no effect line).

`scales` lists a level row's absolute damage figures and `effect_template` is the row with each of them replaced by a positional slot, so the text can be restated at another character level without re-parsing it. See `scaling`.

scaling.note: Every figure in `scales` is what the in-game panel shows a character at `anchor_level`. Damage scales with the character, so figures read at different levels are not comparable - splice two and an upgrade reads as a downgrade. `ratio` is a tree's figure at `anchor_level` divided by the same figure at `low_anchor_level`, measured on rows captured at both. The game truncates rather than rounds, so a stored figure d stands for a true value in [d, d+1). To restate it at level L: floor((d + 0.5) * (1 + (1/ratio - 1) * (anchor_level - L) / (anchor_level - low_anchor_level))). That is exact at both anchors and interpolates between them; outside 9-20 it is extrapolation.
scaling.model_note: `linear` is a straight line between the two anchors, not compounding growth. Both models fit the anchors exactly and diverge by up to 6.7% midway between them, so the data cannot yet separate them - a capture at a third known level would. Linear is preferred because it places the first, unknown-level capture at level 11.9-12.3 in all three trees, against 12.7-13.2 and a wider spread for geometric. Per-level growth under this model is `per_level_of_low_anchor` of the level 9 figure, each level: about 9.1% for Swordmastery and 10.1-10.2% for the other two.
scaling.scaled_rows: Rows marked figure_source: scaled were not read at anchor_level; figure_note records the arithmetic. Rows marked read were.
scaling.first_capture: The registry's original capture was at no single level: its three trees imply levels 11.9, 12.0 and 12.3, so it straddled a level-up. That is why its figures could not be reconciled and why level 20 is the anchor.
scaling.observations_note: Figures read from a panel at a character level other than `anchor_level`, keyed by that level then by ability or perk name then by its level. verify_perks.py restates each `scales` entry at that level through the model and fails if it does not come back to what the panel showed, so the model cannot drift from its evidence. null marks a figure the capture did not show.
scaling.rounding_note: The level 9 panels fix this. Voracious Bite level 4 reads 602 at level 20 where rounding its unit value would give 603, and its level 2 reads 210 at level 9 where rounding the stored 445 gives 211. Truncating (d + 0.5) reproduces all 24 captured figures; rounding d misses one.
